summary:
ASTRA-VITAL is an intelligent health monitoring system designed to protect astronauts' well-being during space missions. It integrates physiological and environmental sensors to collect real-time data, including heart rate, blood oxygen saturation, body temperature, physical activity, sleep patterns, and habitat conditions.

By combining data processing, anomaly detection algorithms, and intelligent analysis, the system identifies potential health risks, detects unusual patterns, and generates alerts to support astronauts and mission control in making informed decisions.

Its architecture combines ESP32-based hardware, local data processing, and a software platform developed with modern technologies. A key feature is its ability to operate autonomously without a constant connection to Earth, processing and storing critical information locally and synchronizing it when communication becomes available.

ASTRA-VITAL aims to move beyond traditional health monitoring by providing an integrated, proactive, and resilient solution that helps anticipate medical complications, improve decision-making, and contribute to safer and more sustainable human space exploration.
details:
ASTRA-VITAL – Project Details

ASTRA-VITAL (Advanced Space Telemetry, Risk Assessment and Vital Intelligence System) is an integrated astronaut health monitoring and decision-support system designed for long-duration space missions and isolated, confined, and extreme (ICE) environments. Developed by Team Ada Lovelace for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, the project addresses the challenges of maintaining crew health when communication with Earth is delayed, limited, or temporarily unavailable.

The system is built around three interconnected subsystems:

1. Embedded Hardware and Sensor Network

ASTRA-VITAL combines two specialized monitoring modules and a central processing unit. The wearable biomedical module collects physiological measurements, including heart rate, blood oxygen saturation (SpO2), electrocardiographic signals (ECG), body temperature, and movement. The environmental monitoring module measures cabin conditions such as CO2 concentration, atmospheric pressure, temperature, humidity, particulate matter, volatile organic compounds (VOCs), and ionizing radiation. An ESP32 microcontroller coordinates sensor acquisition, local data logging, and communication. An OLED display, emergency button, audible alarms, and haptic feedback provide immediate interaction with the crew.

2. Telemetry Backend and Clinical Risk Assessment

A Python-based backend receives and processes sensor readings through a secure REST API. Its clinical rules engine combines predefined physiological thresholds with personalized statistical baselines using Z-Score anomaly detection. This approach allows the system to identify potentially dangerous deviations, distinguish abnormal measurements from individual physiological variations, and generate prioritized alerts. Data validation, API-key authentication, rate limiting, and idempotent storage improve reliability and data integrity.

3. Mission Control and Astronaut Interface

The frontend is a Progressive Web Application (PWA) developed with React, TypeScript, Vite, and Material UI. It provides an operational dashboard for monitoring crew members, viewing physiological and environmental measurements, tracking alerts, and reviewing historical records. Its high-contrast interface, accessibility features, and offline capabilities are designed for demanding operational environments.

Technology and Development Tools

The project uses C++ and Arduino framework for ESP32 firmware, Python 3.11+, Flask 3.x for backend development, SQLite 3 for data persistence, and TypeScript with React 18 for the frontend. Hardware components include ESP32 DevKit V1, MAX30102, AD8232, MLX90614, MPU6050, SCD41, BMP390, SHT31, PMSA003I, SGP40, a Geiger counter, INA219, OLED display, and microSD storage. Git, GitHub, Docker, and automated testing tools support development, integration, and deployment.

Innovation, Benefits, and Intended Impact

ASTRA-VITAL goes beyond conventional health dashboards by combining wearable biomedical monitoring, environmental sensing, edge computing, statistical anomaly detection, and operational decision support in a single architecture. Its main innovation is the integration of astronaut health and habitat conditions, allowing the system to evaluate risks from both physiological and environmental perspectives.

A key design consideration is communication latency during deep-space missions, which can reach approximately 22 minutes one way between Earth and Mars. Instead of depending entirely on continuous communication with mission control, ASTRA-VITAL is designed to process and store critical information locally, maintaining essential monitoring capabilities during communication interruptions.

The team also considered sensor reliability, power consumption, data integrity, cybersecurity, interface accessibility, night-time visibility, medical safety, and the limitations of operating in confined environments.

The intended impact is to support earlier identification of potential health emergencies, reduce dependence on immediate ground-based assistance, improve crew autonomy, and contribute to safer and more sustainable human exploration of the Moon, Mars, and other extreme environments.

ASTRA-VITAL is an engineering prototype and decision-support concept, not a certified medical diagnostic device.

Official GitHub Repository

The source code, technical documentation, and project development are available in the official ASTRA-VITAL repository:

https://github.com/maocorrea1015/Astro-vital
